newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan court confirms Kaneichi liquidation request.
newsitem.headline: Japan court confirms Kaneichi liquidation request.

text.p: The Osaka District Court confirmed reports that property firm Kaneichi had filed for special liquidation at the court on Wednesday.
Credit research firm Teikoku Databank said earlier that the Osaka-based realtor had filed for court liquidation with debts of about 90 billion yen.
The research firm also said that the realtor had borrowed a total of 26.7 billion yen from "jusen" housing loan companies which have now failed.
A spokesman for Osaka District Court confirmed Kaneichi had filed for special liquidation but said he could not give details of the request.
Kaneichi officials were not immediately available for comment.

Teikoku Databank said in a statement that Kaneichi's borrowing snowballed in the late 1980s when Japan's "economic bubble era" of inflated land and stock prices was at its height, but with the end of the boom, it became unable to pay back its debts.
Special liquidation provides a court with more leeway in directing legal procedures than outright bankruptcy, lawyers say.
